messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Greater divergence with more iterations
parts:
This can happen.  It happened with me with the pre-Matt-trick version of the 8 schools model.  One way to get things moving would be to assign the parameter a strong prior distribution and check that all is going ok, then relax the prior if necessary.

This should also motivate us to work on implementing the Cook/Gelman/Rubin "self-cleaning oven," which should be doable now that we have implemented forward simulation in the transformed parameters block.

A

On Jun 24, 2013, at 1:34 PM, jkropko wrote:

Hi,
I'm seeing a strange behavior with my rstan script.  If I run stan for 100 iterations, I see that a particular parameter is nearly converged, with an R-hat of about 1.1.  But if I go to 1000 iterations the R-hat balloons to over 2, and if I go to 10000 iterations the R-hat is over 3.  Does this mean that the early "convergence" is an illusion?  I don't think the model is unidentified, so I also don't understand why the parameter would diverge to a greater extent after so many iterations.  Have you seen this behavior before in any similar situations?
Thanks,
Jon
